## The bug

`ArticleController.create()` is the one handler in the codebase that returns a bare entity instead of the RealWorld envelope.

`src/article/article.controller.ts:51-54`:
```ts
@Post()
async create(@User('id') userId: number, @Body('article') articleData: CreateArticleDto) {
  return this.articleService.create(userId, articleData);   // ← no ArticleRO
}
```

`src/article/article.service.ts:170` declares `Promise<ArticleEntity>` and `src/article/article.service.ts:186` does `return newArticle;`.

So `POST /api/articles` responds with `{ id, slug, title, ... }` — flat. Every other endpoint responds `{ article: {...} }` (`ArticleRO`, `src/article/article.interface.ts:24`). The React client does `response.article.slug`, gets `undefined.slug`, and throws.

**Why the server logs nothing:** from Nest's side the request fully succeeded — the row was inserted and a 201 went out. The crash is entirely client-side, after the response. Nothing to log.

Note the tell: `create()` is the only handler in that controller with no `Promise<*RO>` return annotation. This exact regression is recorded in `LESSONS.md` under issue #57.

## Fix

Keep it in the service, since that's where every other method builds the envelope:

```ts
// article.service.ts:170
async create(userId: number, articleData: CreateArticleDto): Promise<ArticleRO> {
  ...
  const newArticle = await this.articleRepository.save(article);
  ...
  return { article: newArticle };
}
```

and annotate the controller handler `: Promise<ArticleRO>` so the compiler catches the next one.

## Two more bugs in those same 18 lines

While you're in there — both will bite immediately after the crash is fixed:

1. **`body` is never copied.** `create()` sets `title`, `description`, `slug`, `tagList`, `comments` — but not `article.body`, even though `CreateArticleDto` has it (`dto/create-article.dto.ts:4`) and the column defaults to `''` (`article.entity.ts:20`). Every created article saves with an empty body, so the article page renders blank.

2. **The response has no `author`.** `newArticle` is captured at line 179, *before* the author is linked at lines 181-184. The returned object has no `author` relation, so the frontend's byline (`article.author.username`) is the next `undefined` read waiting to happen. Set `article.author = author` before the save rather than relying on `author.articles.push()` — `ArticleEntity.author` is the owning side of that relation, and `UserEntity.articles` (`user.entity.ts:37`) has no cascade.

Want me to apply all three?
